C45008.observed: What was checked: whether pressing the Enter key saves the row, so a technician never has to reach for the mouse. What happened: with a description typed in and the cursor still sitting in the Qty box, pressing Enter saved the part exactly as clicking Save does - the line went from eleven parts to twelve, the "Part added" confirmation appeared, and a fresh empty row opened with the cursor back in Description.

C45009.observed: What was checked: where the Tab key takes you inside the row, and whether it ever escapes the row and drops you somewhere else on the page. What happened: starting in Description, Tab moved to Part number, then Qty, then the Save button, then the Cancel button - and the next Tab came back round to Description again. It stayed inside the row the whole way through and never jumped out to the rest of the page.
C45009.not_observed: The "Pulled from" bin chip is only present while a bin is allocated; bin allocation is covered by the Bin Allocation cases (Story 7) and was not exercised here, so that last Tab stop was not observed.

C45010.observed: What was checked: whether the Escape key closes the row the same way the close control does. What happened: with a new empty row open, pressing Escape closed it straight away. Because there was nothing typed in it there was nothing to lose, so no "are you sure" question was asked - the row simply disappeared, exactly as it does when the close control is used.

C45011.observed: What was checked: what happens when you close a row that you have already typed into. What happened: with a description and a quantity filled in, clicking the row's close control (labelled "Cancel" in Tech view) did not throw the typing away silently. A confirmation appeared first, reading "Discard this part?" with the warning "The details you entered will be lost." and two choices, "Keep Editing" and "Discard Part". Choosing "Discard Part" closed the row and nothing was saved.

C45012.observed: What was checked: whether clicking somewhere else on the page throws away a row you are part-way through filling in. What happened: with "ZZAUTOTEST tv outside" in the description and 4 in the quantity, clicking on the page well away from the row left the row exactly where it was - still open, still showing both values, with no confirmation asked and nothing lost. A stray click cannot cost the technician their typing.

C45019.observed: What was checked: whether an untouched row is closed instantly, without a needless confirmation. What happened: with a brand new row open and nothing typed into it, clicking the row's close control (labelled "Cancel" in Tech view) closed it immediately, and pressing Escape on an empty row did the same. Neither one asked a question first, because there was nothing entered that could be lost.
